summary: This defines a Room class: a simple blueprint for one room in a house, holding its name, length, and width. It follows the standard Java pattern of private fields with public getters and setters, plus a toString method so a room can be printed.

lines.text: The class is the blueprint; each Room object created from it represents one real room, such as a kitchen or a bedroom.
The room's name is stored as text, and marking it private means only code inside Room can touch it directly.
Length is a double because room measurements are rarely whole numbers, so decimals like 12.5 must be allowed.
This no-argument constructor lets you create an empty Room first and fill in the values later with the setters.

lines.text: The second constructor takes all three values at once, so a fully described room can be built in a single statement.
The parameter and the field share the name "name", so this.name makes it clear that the field of this object is being assigned.
A getter gives outside code read access to a private field, which keeps the class in control of its own data.
A setter is the only way outside code can change the field, which is where validation rules could be added later.
This annotation tells the compiler you intend to replace a method inherited from Object, so a typo in the method name becomes an error instead of a silent bug.
Every object inherits a toString from Object that prints something unreadable, so replacing it means printing a Room shows its actual field values.
The escaped \' places single quotes around the name in the output, making it obvious that the name is text.
